messages.author: 52132a509bbe5f1a
messages.subject: memory problem - extractRawCopyNumbers
parts:
Hi,

I am doing paired analysis on SNP 6 data. All I want is to compute the
standard deviation of raw copy numbers for each pair and store the
results in a file. The following code does exactly this. HOWEVER, the
memory usage keeps growing as j increments -- 3.5 GB is used up when j
reaches about 53, which is not logical to me at all because all
variables should be reused every loop. This is no good because I have
hundreds of arrays and I will need to add another loop outside the j-
loop.

p.s. i had tried to use local variables instead of global (<- instead
of <<-) inside for-loops (instead of sapply) but that didn't work
either. Those "rm"s and "gc"s were some desperate moves which didn't
work either.

Please advise...

===================================================

cbs <<- CbsModel (cesCase, ces2)

#for (j in 1:length(cesCase$files)) {
jLoop=function(j) {

rawCNsAll <<- c()

#for (k in 1:23) {
kLoop=function(k) {

rawCNs <<- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=j, chromosome=k)$cn
rawCNsAll <<- c(rawCNsAll,rawCNs)

rm(rawCNs)
gc()

print(paste("k",k))
return(k)

}
tmpk<<-sapply(1:23,kLoop)

stdev <<- sd(rawCNsAll,na.rm=T)
sdRecordCurRow <<- data.frame(sample=cesCase$Names[j],stdev)

write.table(sdRecordCurRow,sdRecordFnameTmp,sep=",",row.names=F,col.names=F,append=T)

rm(stdev)
rm(sdRecordCurRow)
rm(rawCNsAll)
gc()

print(paste("j",j))
return (j)

}
tmpj <<- sapply(1:length(cesCase$files),jLoop)

messages.author: 9dda904b2c7a149c
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] memory problem - extractRawCopyNumbers
parts:
Hi Jason,

First of all, I would strongly recommend against using global variables inside functions, unless there is a really good reason for doing so.  It is very dangerous programming practice.  In fact, in your example, there isn't any need for global assignments at all so it would be best to steer clear of them.

You don't have to use sapply() (which is s-l-o-w) in your case - ordinary loop structures should work fine.  In fact I now notice that you did try using local variables and not using sapply - was your code anything like this?:

for (j in 1:length(cesCase$files)) {
  rawCNsAll <- c()
 
  for (k in 1:23) {

rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=j, chromosome=k)$cn
      rawCNsAll <- c(rawCNsAll, rawCNs)

  }

stdev <- sd(rawCNsAll, na.rm=T)
  sdRecordCurRow <- data.frame(sample=cesCase$Names[j], stdev)

 write.table(sdRecordCurRow,sdRecordFnameTmp,sep=",",row.names=F,col.names=F,append=T)
  print(paste("j", j))

}

If not, could you please try this and see if you get the same increase in memory usage?  I have tried the code you posted but with random numbers instead of real output from extractRawCopyNumbers() and see no increase, and similarly, the code above does not result in increased memory usage with random numbers.  If the above still results in high memory usage then the problem may be with extractRawCopyNumbers() or with your setup (you didn't give us a sessionInfo() or traceback() - were there any warnings etc.?).

Cheers,

Ken

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: memory problem - extractRawCopyNumbers
parts:
Hi,

extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs) caches the results *in memory* in the 'cbs'
object. This is why you run out of memory. By calling gc(cbs), you
will clear the cache of the 'cbs' object. I suggest you do this
immediately after and each time you are calling
extractRawCopyNumbers(), e.g.

rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=j, chromosome=k)$cn;
gc(cbs);

FYI, the extractRawCopyNumbers() was added as an ad hoc solution in
the beginning, which is probably why the results are cached by
default. In the next release there will be an argument 'cache=FALSE'
so that you have to extractRawCopyNumbers(..., cache=TRUE) if you
really want to cache the results (in memory).

Cheers

Henrik
